threads.thread_goal: Align on current journey map, key gaps, and overall pathway design.

messages.text: Hi team, I've completed the initial mapping of our current client journey from referral through to employment. I reviewed 12 recent cases and documented the main stages and handoff points. The visual map and gap analysis are now in the shared drive linked to T1. Key patterns emerged: clients often wait 3-4 weeks between assessment and skills planning, and there's minimal coordination between our social work assessments and employment support intake. I've also sketched a first version of the new pathway structure in A1 that tries to compress these stages and clarify roles. Would appreciate your feedback on whether this captures the right flow.

Thanks for this, really clear mapping. I've looked at the journey and the new pathway sketch. One thing I notice is that the employment readiness workshops sit quite late in the flow—after health screening. I'm wondering if we should move some of the basic workshop content earlier, maybe even during the initial assessment phase, so clients get a sense of what's possible before they're fully screened. This could help with engagement. Also, the handoff from social work to employment support in your map still looks a bit fuzzy. Should we define explicit trigger points and a standard handover note template as part of T6?

Good points from 76106. I agree the handoff clarity is critical—we've had clients slip through before because nobody was sure who was responsible at transition points. On the workshop timing, I'd lean toward keeping the health screening first, but maybe we can do a brief orientation session right after initial assessment that explains the pathway and sets expectations. That way clients aren't waiting passively. I'll start drafting the coordination protocol in T6 and will include a simple handover checklist. Should have something for review by EOD tomorrow.

I think the orientation idea makes sense. For the workshops themselves, I'm still working through the outline in T3, but I want to make sure we're clear on what 'employment readiness' actually means for our clients. Looking at the gaps you identified, it seems like some clients need basic job search skills, others need confidence building, and some need help with workplace behaviour. Should we design the workshops as modular so different clients can take different paths? Or do we run everyone through the same core sessions? This will affect how we structure the content.

That's a fair question. I think we need to balance flexibility with simplicity—we only have 21 days to pilot this. My suggestion: design 3-4 core sessions that everyone does (covering pathway overview, job search basics, workplace expectations, and managing transitions), then offer optional follow-up modules based on individual assessment outcomes. This keeps the pilot manageable but still responsive to client needs. Does that feel workable for T3?

I wanted to flag something on the health screening side. Before clients move into the pathway, we need to make sure we're catching any physical or mental health issues that might affect their ability to engage. I'm drafting T4 now—a short screening checklist that social workers can use during initial assessment. It will flag things like mobility concerns, medication side effects, or anxiety that might need support. Once I have a draft, I'll need input from social work on how this integrates with your assessment process.

On the logistics side, I'm thinking about T5—the safe move checklist. The pathway mentions clients moving to new accommodation and then to workplaces. I need to understand the sequence better. Do clients move homes first, settle in, then start employment? Or do some moves happen in parallel? This affects how I plan the checklist and what support we need to coordinate with social work.

Good question. In most cases, clients will be in stable housing before we start employment support—that's part of the vulnerability profile. But some may be transitioning housing during the pathway. I think for the pilot, we should assume housing is stable first, then focus on workplace transitions. We can refine this based on pilot experience. 459543, can you draft T5 with that assumption and we'll validate it once we have real client profiles?

I'm also thinking about the overall pathway stages. From what I'm hearing, it sounds like we're converging on something like: 1) Initial assessment + orientation, 2) Health screening, 3) Core workshops, 4) Employer matching and placement prep, 5) Workplace transition and follow-up. Is that the right sequence? If so, we should lock this in as D1 so everyone's designing their pieces to fit the same flow.

Yes, that sequence makes sense to me. I'd add one thing: between health screening and workshops, we should have a brief care planning session where social work and employment support sit down with the client and agree on goals and any support adjustments needed. This becomes the reference point for the rest of the pathway. I can include this in T6 as a formal handover point.

Agreed. So D1 is: Main pathway stages are (1) Initial assessment + orientation, (2) Health screening, (3) Care planning session, (4) Core workshops, (5) Employer matching and placement prep, (6) Workplace transition and follow-up. Everyone designing to this flow. Now, on D2—the top 3 priority gaps we want to address. From T1, the recurring issues were: long wait times between assessment and action, unclear handoffs, and clients not understanding what to expect. I'd say our top 3 are: (a) compress timelines by running assessment and orientation in parallel, (b) define explicit handover points and shared case summaries, (c) create clear client-facing information so people know what's coming. Does that align with what you're seeing?

Those three gaps feel right. I'd add that the client-facing information piece (gap c) is also about accessibility—we need materials that work for people with low literacy or language barriers. I'm planning to draft T7 with that in mind. Plain language, visuals, maybe a short video walkthrough if we have time. This ties directly to the inclusion theme in the project brief.

I think we're in a good place on D1 and D2. Let me summarise: D1 locked—six-stage pathway with care planning as a formal handover. D2 locked—top gaps are timeline compression, handover clarity, and accessible client information. Now I need to make sure T3 (workshop outline) is designed to fit this flow and support these gaps. I'll have a first draft by tomorrow afternoon. One question though: should the workshops include any content on managing stress or dealing with setbacks? Some of our clients have trauma histories and might need that framing.

Absolutely. That should be woven into the workshops, especially in the first session where we set expectations and build psychological safety. I'd suggest framing it as 'managing the employment journey' rather than 'trauma' to keep it accessible and non-stigmatising. 14638, this is also where the health screening and care planning become important—we'll know more about each client's needs before the workshops start, so we can tailor the tone and content.
That makes sense. I'll make sure T4 includes questions about mental health support needs and any trauma-informed care flags. Then I can brief the workshop facilitators on what to watch for.

Great. So to wrap TH1: we've agreed on D1 (six-stage pathway) and D2 (three priority gaps). Next steps are clear: 9716 finalises T6 (coordination protocol) by EOD tomorrow, 6627 drafts T3 (workshop outline) by tomorrow afternoon, 76106 starts T7 (client info pack), and 14638 continues T4 (health screening). I'll refine A1 (pathway overview) to reflect the agreed stages and share by end of day. Everyone good with this?

Sounds good. I'll keep working on T5 (safe move checklist) in parallel. Once I see the final pathway stages and care planning details, I can make sure the move checklist aligns with the transition points.

Perfect. I think we've made solid progress on the overall design. D1 and D2 are locked, and everyone has clear next steps. Let's reconvene in TH2 once the assessment template, health checklist, and safeguarding flow are ready for review.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise assessment, health screening, and safeguarding tools.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the holistic assessment and consent checklist (A2) based on our agreed pathway stages. It covers social, health, employment, and safeguarding dimensions, plus a clear consent section that explains data sharing and client rights. The template is designed to be completed during the initial assessment session and then referenced throughout the pathway. I've also started T2 to document the assessment process itself. Would appreciate review from 6627 and 14638 on whether this captures what you need from your roles.

Thanks for this. I've reviewed A2 and it looks comprehensive. I've also drafted T4—the health screening checklist. It's a short form that flags physical health, mental health, medication, mobility, and safeguarding concerns. The idea is that I or a social worker can use this during or right after the initial assessment to identify any health barriers to employment. I've included referral triggers so we know when to escalate to clinical services. Can you review T4 and let me know if the health questions integrate well with your assessment template?

I've looked at T4 and it integrates well. The health questions don't duplicate what's in A2, they just go deeper on specific health flags. I'd suggest we add a line in A2 that says 'Health screening completed via T4 checklist' so there's a clear link between the two documents. Also, I notice T4 asks about medication—should we have a field in A2 for 'current support needs' that references the health screening output? That way the care planning session in stage 3 has all the info it needs.

I've reviewed both A2 and T4 as well. They look solid. One thing I want to flag: in the employment readiness workshops (T3), we'll be asking clients about their work history, skills, and barriers. Some of that overlaps with what's in A2. Should we be explicit about what information we're gathering in assessment vs. what we're exploring in the workshops? Otherwise clients might feel like they're repeating themselves.

Good catch. The assessment in A2 is more about 'what do we need to know to support this person?' The workshops are about 'what does this person want to explore about their own employment journey?' So there will be some overlap, but the framing is different. I think we can add a note in A2 that says something like 'This assessment captures baseline information. The workshops will help clients explore their own goals and strengths in more depth.' That way it's clear they're complementary, not redundant.

I want to bring in the safeguarding piece now. I've drafted T9—the safeguarding and incident reporting flow. It defines what counts as an incident (abuse, neglect, exploitation, self-harm, safeguarding concerns), the reporting steps, timelines, and escalation path. It's aligned with our organisational safeguarding policy. The key thing is that every role needs to know when and how to report. I've included a simple decision tree so staff can quickly figure out if something needs to be reported. Can everyone review T9 and flag any gaps?

I've reviewed T9 and the decision tree is clear. One thing I'd add: what happens if a client discloses something during a workshop that raises safeguarding concerns? The flow should specify that the workshop facilitator pauses, documents what was said, and immediately escalates to the social worker. We need to make sure there's no gap between disclosure and action.

Excellent point. I'll add a specific section on 'disclosures during group activities' to T9. Now, I also want to propose A7—the safeguarding and incident reporting flow as a visual guide. It will be a one-page flowchart that staff can print and keep at their desk. This makes it easier to reference quickly when something comes up. I'll draft this by EOD today.

I have a question about T4 and safeguarding. If the health screening flags something like self-harm or suicidal ideation, does that automatically trigger the safeguarding flow in T9? Or is there a separate clinical pathway? I want to make sure I'm not missing anything.

Good question. If T4 flags mental health crisis (active suicidal ideation, acute psychosis, etc.), that's a clinical escalation first—we'd refer to mental health services immediately. Once the client is stabilised, then we assess whether they're ready for the employment pathway. If T4 flags lower-level mental health concerns (depression, anxiety, past trauma), that goes into the care planning session and we adjust support accordingly. I'll clarify this in T9 so there's no confusion about when it's clinical vs. safeguarding.

So to summarise where we are on D3 and D4: A2 (assessment template) is ready pending the small updates we discussed—adding the health screening link and the note about workshops being complementary. T4 (health screening) is solid. T9 (safeguarding flow) needs the disclosure section added and clarification on clinical vs. safeguarding escalation. A7 (visual safeguarding guide) will be drafted by EOD. Once those updates are done, I think we can approve D3 (assessment template and consent checklist for pilot use) and D4 (safeguarding and incident reporting flow). Does that sound right?

I agree. I'd just add one more thing: once A2 is finalised, we should do a quick test run with a volunteer client or a case study to make sure the assessment actually takes a reasonable amount of time and doesn't feel overwhelming. Same with T4. We have 21 days to pilot, so we need to know these tools are practical.
Good idea. I can do a test run of A2 with a recent case file by tomorrow EOD. 14638, can you do the same with T4? That way we'll know if there are any timing or clarity issues before we roll it out.
I'll do the test run tomorrow. I'll also check that the referral triggers in T4 are clear and that I know who to contact if something needs escalation.

I'll have A7 (visual safeguarding guide) and the updated T9 with disclosure section ready by EOD today. Once everyone's done their test runs and updates, we can lock D3 and D4. I think we're on track.

Sounds good. Once D3 and D4 are locked, we'll have a solid foundation for the rest of the pathway. Next up is TH3 where we finalise the workshops and client info pack. I'm on track with T7 (client-facing info pack) and should have a draft by tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Shape the workshop programme and client-facing information pack.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the employment readiness workshop outline (T3) with four core sessions: Session 1 is 'Your Employment Journey'—setting expectations, building psychological safety, and introducing the pathway. Session 2 is 'Skills and Strengths'—helping clients identify what they can do and what they want to do. Session 3 is 'Job Search and Workplace Basics'—practical skills like CV writing, interview prep, and workplace behaviour. Session 4 is 'Managing Transitions'—dealing with setbacks, building resilience, and planning next steps. Each session is 2 hours with breaks, and I've designed activities that work for mixed literacy levels. I've also drafted a client feedback form so we can gather input after each session. Would appreciate feedback from 8393 and 76106 on whether this structure fits the pathway and whether the content is accessible.

I've reviewed T3 and the structure is solid. The four sessions flow logically and the activities look engaging. One thing I'd suggest: in Session 1, add a section on 'What support is available to you?' so clients know they can ask for help if they're struggling. Also, I notice the feedback form is quite detailed—might be too much for clients to fill out after a 2-hour session. Could we simplify it to 3-4 key questions? I'm also working on T7 (client info pack) and I want to make sure the workshop description in there matches what you've designed.

Good points. I'll add the support section to Session 1 and simplify the feedback form to 3-4 questions. What are the key things you want to know from clients after each session? That will help me design the feedback form.

I'd focus on: (1) Did you understand the content? (2) Was the pace okay? (3) What was most useful? (4) What would you change? Those four questions give us enough to iterate without overwhelming people.

I've reviewed T3 as well and I think it's well-designed. The four sessions align with the pathway stages we agreed on. One thing I want to flag: in Session 2 ('Skills and Strengths'), we'll be asking clients to reflect on their abilities. Some of our clients have low confidence or past negative work experiences. Make sure the facilitator is trained to validate their experiences and help them see strengths even if they don't see them in themselves. This ties back to the trauma-informed approach we discussed.

Absolutely. I'll add facilitator notes for each session that highlight the trauma-informed approach and give examples of how to validate and reframe. I'll also include a section on 'what to do if a client becomes distressed' so facilitators know how to respond.

Perfect. Now, on T7 (client info pack), I've drafted a plain-language leaflet that explains the pathway, what to expect in each stage, client rights, and how data will be used. I've kept sentences short, used simple words, and included some visuals to break up the text. I've also drafted a one-page summary that clients can take home. The full pack includes the pathway overview, the workshop schedule, contact information, and a FAQ section. Can you review T7 and let me know if the workshop description matches what you've designed?

I've reviewed T7 and the workshop description is accurate. The language is accessible and the visuals help. One thing I'd add: in the FAQ section, include a question like 'What if I'm worried about something?' with an answer that points to the support resources. This ties back to the support section I'm adding to Session 1.

I've also reviewed T7 and it looks good. The plain language is clear and the structure is logical. One thing I want to check: does the info pack mention anything about the assessment process and what information we'll be collecting? Clients should know upfront what we're asking and why.

Good catch. I've included a section on 'Initial Assessment' that explains we'll be asking about social, health, and employment needs, and that we'll be asking for consent to share information with the team. But I could expand this a bit to be more specific about what we're collecting and why. I'll add more detail to T7.

I want to make sure the info pack also mentions safeguarding and what happens if we have concerns. Clients should know that we're here to protect them and that we'll involve them in any decisions about their safety. I can draft some language for this if that helps.
That would be really helpful. I'll add a section on 'Your Safety and Rights' that includes the language you draft. This ties back to the safeguarding flow we finalised in TH2.

So where are we on D5 and D6? I think T3 is ready to lock pending the updates I mentioned (support section in Session 1, simplified feedback form, facilitator notes on trauma-informed approach). T7 looks solid pending the additions from 9716 on safeguarding language and more detail on assessment. Once those are done, I think we can approve D5 (lock workshop structure and topics) and D6 (sign off client info pack).

I agree. I'll incorporate 9716's safeguarding language and expand the assessment section in T7 by EOD today. 6627, can you have the updated T3 with the support section and facilitator notes ready by tomorrow morning? Then we can lock both D5 and D6.

I'll have the updated T3 ready by tomorrow morning. I'll also make sure the workshop schedule is realistic—we need to fit four 2-hour sessions into the pilot timeline without overwhelming clients or staff.

I'll draft the safeguarding language for T7 by EOD today. I want to make sure it's clear and reassuring without being scary. Something like 'We're here to keep you safe. If we have concerns about your wellbeing, we'll talk to you about it and work together on solutions.'

That language is good. Clear and collaborative. Once T3 and T7 are finalised, we'll have D5 and D6 locked. Then we move to TH4 to sort out the logistics—moves, workplace transitions, and employer engagement. 459543, are you ready to present the safe move checklist?

I'm working on T5 now. I'll have a draft ready for TH4. I've been thinking about the sequence of moves and workplace transitions, and I want to make sure the checklist covers both home moves and first-day workplace support.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on logistics for moves, workplace transitions, and employer engagement.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the safe relocation and workplace transition checklist (T5). It covers three main areas: (1) Pre-move planning—understanding the client's needs, arranging transport, checking the new space; (2) Move day—protecting dignity and belongings, managing stress, documenting what's moved; (3) Post-move and workplace transition—first-day support, follow-up check-ins, handling any issues. The checklist is designed to be practical and respectful. I've included prompts for movers to check in with clients about their comfort and concerns. I've also built in a section where social workers can flag any specific needs or sensitivities. Would appreciate feedback from 8393 and 76106 on whether this covers what you need.

I've reviewed T5 and it's comprehensive. The three-phase structure makes sense. One thing I want to flag: in the pre-move planning phase, we need to make sure the social worker has done the care planning session (stage 3 of the pathway) before the move happens. That way we know about any health or wellbeing needs that might affect how the move is managed. Can you add a line in T5 that says 'Confirm care plan is complete before scheduling move'?

Good point. I'll add that. I'll also add a section where the mover can document any concerns that come up during the move—like if a client seems distressed or if there are physical barriers we didn't anticipate. That way the social worker knows to follow up.

I've also reviewed T5. The structure is good. I'm thinking about the workplace transition part—after the move, clients will be starting employment. We need to make sure there's coordination between the mover, the social worker, and the employment support worker. Should T5 include a handover to employment support that flags any concerns or needs that came up during the move?

Absolutely. I'll add a section at the end of T5 that's a handover note to employment support. It will include: client's mood and confidence, any physical or emotional concerns, what went well, what was challenging, and any follow-up needed. This ties back to the coordination protocol we finalised in TH1.
Perfect. Now, on the employer side, 76106, do you have an update on T11 (identifying community employers)? We need to confirm at least 3 employers for the pilot.

I've been working on T11 and I've identified 5 potential employers: a local cafe, a community garden project, a charity shop, a small manufacturing firm, and a care home. I've had initial conversations with three of them and they're interested in hosting placements. I'm still waiting to hear back from the other two. I'm documenting each employer's profile—what kind of work they offer, how many placements they can take, what support they need from us. I should have the full list and confirmations by EOD tomorrow.

Great. Once you have the confirmations, we'll need to brief the employers on the pathway and what support we can offer them. We should also clarify expectations—like how often we'll check in, what to do if there's an issue, and how we'll handle it if a placement doesn't work out. Can you draft a simple employer briefing document as part of T11?

I'll draft an employer briefing document that covers: what the pathway is, what we're asking of them, what support we'll provide, how we'll communicate, and what happens if there are issues. I'll keep it simple and practical.

I want to make sure the employer briefing also includes information about the clients—like, what kinds of support needs they might have, how to create an inclusive workplace, and what to do if a client is struggling. We don't want employers to be surprised or unprepared.

Good point. I'll include a section on 'Supporting our clients' that covers common needs, reasonable adjustments, and how to communicate with us if there are concerns. I'll also include contact information for the social worker and employment support worker assigned to each client.

I want to flag something on safeguarding. If an employer has concerns about a client—like if they're worried about abuse or exploitation—they need to know how to report it. Can we include a safeguarding section in the employer briefing that explains the reporting process?
Absolutely. I'll include a section on 'Safeguarding and Reporting' that explains what to watch for and how to contact us if there are concerns. I'll keep it simple and non-alarmist, but clear.

So where are we on D7 and D8? I think T5 is ready to lock pending the updates 459543 mentioned (care plan confirmation, concerns documentation, handover to employment support). T11 is on track with confirmations by EOD tomorrow and an employer briefing document. Once those are done, we can approve D7 (safe relocation and workplace transition checklist) and D8 (confirm initial set of employers).
I'll have the updated T5 ready by tomorrow morning. I want to make sure the checklist is practical and doesn't add too much burden to the mover's day.
I'll have the employer confirmations and briefing document ready by EOD tomorrow. Once we have those, we can lock D7 and D8 and move to TH5 to set up tracking and evaluation.

Good. So next steps: 459543 finalises T5 by tomorrow morning, 76106 confirms employers and drafts briefing by EOD tomorrow. Then we'll lock D7 and D8 and move to TH5 for tracking and evaluation setup.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, evaluation, and team rituals for the pilot.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the pilot outcome and attendance tracker (A6) and the evaluation plan (T12). A6 is a simple spreadsheet that tracks: client pseudonym, attendance at each workshop, milestones reached (assessment complete, health screening done, care plan agreed, first day at work), and employment outcomes (placement secured, duration, any issues). Client identifiers are pseudonymised to protect privacy. T12 outlines the evaluation approach: we'll track attendance and milestones, gather client feedback after each workshop, do a mid-pilot check-in at day 10, and a final review at day 21. We'll also collect staff feedback on what's working and what needs adjustment. The goal is to have enough data to show whether the pilot is on track and what to improve for scaling. Would appreciate feedback on whether these tools capture what we need.

I've reviewed A6 and T12. The tracker is clear and the pseudonymisation approach is good. One thing I'd add to A6: a column for 'support adjustments made' so we can track if we changed anything based on client needs or feedback. This will help us understand what adaptations were most helpful. Also, in T12, I'd suggest we do a quick team check-in at day 7 (not just day 10) to catch any early issues and adjust quickly.
Good suggestions. I'll add the 'support adjustments' column to A6 and add a day 7 check-in to T12. This will give us more granular data on what's working.

I've also reviewed A6 and T12. I want to make sure we're capturing safeguarding incidents and any concerns that come up during the pilot. Should we have a separate log for incidents, or should they be noted in A6?

Good point. I think incidents should be logged separately using the safeguarding flow we finalised in TH2 (A7). But in A6, we could add a column that flags 'safeguarding concern raised' so we can see at a glance if there were any issues. The detailed incident log would be separate.

I've reviewed A6 and T12 as well. The evaluation plan is solid. One thing I want to check: are we planning to gather feedback from employers as well? They'll have insights into how clients are doing in the workplace and whether the pathway is preparing them well.

That's a great point. I'll add an employer feedback section to T12. We can do a brief check-in with each employer at day 10 and a final debrief at day 21. I'll draft a simple feedback form for employers.

I want to make sure we're also tracking health and wellbeing outcomes. In A6, should we have a column for 'health concerns flagged' or 'health support provided'? This will help us understand if the health screening and care planning are working.
Good idea. I'll add a column for 'health support provided' so we can track what adjustments or referrals were made based on the health screening. This ties back to the care planning session.
Now, on T10 (staff training), we need to make sure everyone is trained on the new pathway before we launch. 14638, I think you were going to coordinate this. What's the plan?

I'm working on T10 now. The plan is to do short training sessions embedded in normal shifts—so people don't have to take time out of their day. I'm planning three sessions: (1) Pathway overview and roles, (2) Using the assessment and health screening tools, (3) Safeguarding and incident reporting. Each session is 30 minutes. I'll schedule them for next week so we have time to train everyone before the pilot launches. I'll send out invites and materials by EOD tomorrow.

Good plan. Make sure the training materials are clear and practical. People need to know not just what the tools are, but how to use them in their day-to-day work. Also, can you include a Q&A section at the end of each session so people can ask questions?

Absolutely. I'll build in time for Q&A and I'll also set up a rolling Q&A thread in the channel for people to ask questions asynchronously. That way people who can't make the live sessions can still get answers.

So where are we on D9 and D10? I think A6 and T12 are ready to lock pending the updates we discussed (support adjustments column, day 7 check-in, employer feedback, health support column). T10 is on track with training sessions scheduled for next week. Once those are done, we can approve D9 (agree on key indicators and data to track) and D10 (confirm cadence and format of check-ins).

I agree. Let me summarise D9 and D10: D9 is that we'll track attendance, milestones, support adjustments, health support, safeguarding concerns, and employment outcomes. D10 is that we'll do check-ins at day 7, day 10, and day 21, with a final retrospective at the end. Does that capture it?
Yes, that's right. I'll update A6 and T12 with all the changes we discussed and have them ready by EOD today. 14638, can you have T10 (training sessions and materials) ready by EOD tomorrow?
I'll have T10 ready by EOD tomorrow. I'll include the training schedule, materials, and the Q&A thread setup.

Once we have D9 and D10 locked, we'll have all the major decisions made. The pilot is ready to launch. I think we should do a final team sync to make sure everyone knows their role and the timeline. Can we schedule that for early next week?

Good idea. Let's schedule a final sync for Monday morning to review all the tools, confirm roles, and set the launch date. I'll send out a calendar invite. In the meantime, everyone should have their deliverables ready by EOD tomorrow so we can do a final review over the weekend.
